# Compiler Factory — Studio 0.19.0

## Open and run

Click **Run Code** in the existing editor. The original IDE remains available;
the separate Run window now contains the integrated Compiler Factory. Allow
popups for Studio. If a popup is blocked, click **Open the factory in a new tab**
in the editor notice. This alternative opens the same authenticated Run view.
It still requires the browser to allow a user-initiated tab.

The entry source and project files are captured together when Run is clicked.
The paper preview, compiler, VM and report all use that captured snapshot.
Editing in the IDE marks the older factory snapshot as changed; it does not
change a program already waiting or running. Use **Run again** for new source.

The real existing compiler runs immediately in its Worker. The journey presents
its recorded events at a readable pace. After all six phases pass, the existing
VM waits for the package to reach the execution environment, or for **Run now**.
Compilation errors never unlock this handoff. A one-shot gate checks the run ID.

## The six rooms

| Room | Actual compiler evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Lexical analysis | Tokens and source positions from the existing lexer |
| Syntax analysis | The existing parser's returned tree, before imports expand |
| AST generation | The expanded AST, before semantic elaboration |
| Semantic analysis | Resolved declarations, signatures and library imports |
| Code generation | Real JBC2/JBC3 instruction disassembly and instruction count |
| Asset validation | Required workspace resources and real asset warnings |

The room order is the existing compiler's order. Runtime is a separate final
environment, not an invented seventh compilation phase. Missing assets block
execution even if bytecode was already generated.

| AST Tree | Inspect actual expanded AST nodes with the same controls |
| Compilation Report | Actual statuses, measured timings, errors, warnings, artifact counts, source hash and JSON download |

Start, Pause, Resume, Restart and Previous/Next Phase control presentation.
They do not claim to suspend or rerun an already completed compilation.
Restart replays the captured journey; it cannot execute the same VM twice.
**Stop** terminates the real Worker. **Run again** recompiles the current editor.
Reset Camera, Zoom In/Out and Auto Camera change the 3D viewpoint. Drag or use
arrow keys on the canvas; Home resets it. Select a room to pause and inspect it.

When a compiler phase fails, the package stops in that room, its status and

The report's phase timings are measured by the existing compiler. That compiler

## Preserved runtime behavior

Console text comes from real VM print hooks. Input uses the original request /
accept bridge. Games use the existing Renderer, actual VM snapshots, key/mouse
events, audio and 60 Hz simulated tick request. Debug starts with the existing
Debug button and retains Continue, Step Into/Over/Out, breakpoints, call stack,
locals and source navigation. The terminal stays readable after completion.
Clearing the visible console does not remove the report's captured output;
typed input echoes are excluded from the program-output field.

The original compiler grammar, semantic analyzer, code generator, VM, game
engine, native C++ source, native executables and classifier model are retained.
Integration edits add tree capture to compiler-trace, authenticated factory
events to run-window, and the execution handoff/timing to worker. The original
3D Lab learning view and all professional tools from 0.18 remain available.
No inference service, model installation, Ollama or API key is introduced.

# Jimsabz Studio 0.18.0 — professional development tools

Studio 0.18.0 extends all eight requested areas. The compiler grammar, semantic
analysis, stack VM, native binaries and separate interactive Run window retain
their existing implementation. Studio version and language version are separate:
this package contains native compiler/runtime 0.8.0 and the implemented v3 preview
with its v2.6 baseline. The creator's original v2.5 brief is not a conformance claim.

## Open the tools

Choose **Develop**, or press **Ctrl Shift P**. Tabs open Code tools, Tests,
Recovery, Source control, Scene & assets, and Windows release. The left rail
also opens frequently used tools. Run Code continues to open a second window.

## 1. Compiler-backed editor assistance

The active entry and its imported files are compiled in a separate analysis
worker after a short typing delay. The live indicator opens actual diagnostics,
including their code, file, line and column. Analysis does not execute source or
alter the Build/Run pipeline. A timeout stops expensive analysis workers.

The parser provides declarations, lexical scopes, source locations and function
parameters. Editor completion uses this information and existing language
snippets. Hover over a known name for its type/signature. The lower editor strip
shows symbol or call information.

- F12: go to a known definition.
- Shift F12: list bound references.
- F2: preview and apply a symbol rename.
- Alt Shift F: format indentation.

Safe rename supports variables, constants, parameters and unambiguous free
functions. It checks collisions, stale source and compiler validity before
enabling Apply. Generic functions, overloaded names, fields and class renames
are deliberately not rewritten. Named-argument parameter renames are refused.
Advanced binding/navigation is limited; this is an in-product language service,

not an LSP server or a claim that every v3 refactoring is implemented.

Formatting reindents source without merging statements or changing newline
termination. It preserves tokens and multiline comment contents. A checkpoint
is saved before applying formatting or a reviewed rename.

## 2. Broader local agent planning

The existing trained classifier and generators remain available. No model
service, API key or Ollama installation is required. The classifier is reused
from the 0.14 training run; there is no new neural model training in 0.18.

A new compositional numeric planner combines requested operations:

- Total, average, minimum and maximum.
- Ascending/descending heapsort and median.
- Search for a specified value, or ask for a search value at runtime.
- Literal arrays, requested counts from 1 through 1,000, or a runtime count.
- Separate main source and reusable calculation module.
- Optional report saving to a requested `.txt` filename.
- Follow-up requests that preserve previous operations and edit the known generated
  source/module pair in place. If source was customized, a separate draft preserves it.

Try: `Write a program for 12 numbers with total, median, maximum and sorting`.
Then: `Add minimum and search for 42`.

An interactive calculator supports +, -, *, / and division-by-zero handling.
These builders compile and execute sample expected-output fixtures in the real
VM. Failed checks disable Apply. The existing staged review, reject and undo
workflow remains in place. Unsupported open-ended synthesis remains outside the
local classifier/planner's scope. The agent is not an unrestricted generative LLM.

## 3. Windows release tooling

EXE export uses the existing native runtime and embeds bytecode and referenced
assets. Packaged game resources retain the existing asset pipeline. Native FileSystem

operations read/write the separate per-program user-data directory. An arbitrary
project text file is not automatically seeded into that directory. Programs that
need initial user-data files must create them explicitly.

Run `npm run test:release` for runtime integrity, PE64 export and checksum tests.
On Windows x64 it also executes exported console/input/module/array/file examples
from empty directories and compares exact output. On other hosts those execution
checks report **Not Run**.

On Windows, run:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/test-windows-release.ps1
```

The GitHub workflow runs the same checks on a Windows Server 2022 runner. This
does not substitute for Windows 10/11 client installation, graphics and audio
checks. The workflow is supplied but was not executed in this development session.

The Inno Setup recipe installs the desktop app for the current user, supplies
Start-menu/optional desktop shortcuts, records version 0.18.0 and provides an
uninstaller. It leaves user project folders outside the installation directory.
Install Inno Setup on your Windows release machine, then run:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/build-release.ps1
```

Optional parameters `-CertificateThumbprint`, `-SignTool` and `-TimestampUrl`
sign and verify the final installer with the publisher's own certificate.
No certificate or private key is shipped. Signing does not guarantee immediate
SmartScreen reputation. Rebuilding/signing the native binaries is a separate
release step; the bundled native files are unchanged in this release.

Recorded Windows execution, installer compilation/installation and publisher
signing remain **Not Run** until carried out on the appropriate Windows host.
The Windows release tab states these limits and displays saved evidence.

## 4. Recovery, history and local folder saving

The existing browser workspace database is retained. A separate IndexedDB vault
stores cloned checkpoints. Automatic checkpoints are throttled; manual and
before-change checkpoints capture reviewed operations. Retention is up to 40
snapshots / 32 MiB per project, with a 16 MiB snapshot limit. Older snapshots are
pruned automatically. Export a ZIP backup for independent long-term storage.

A small synchronous write-ahead journal covers source edits between keystrokes
and the asynchronous save. On reopening, a differing journal entry is offered for
review. Recovery/restoration creates a checkpoint of current source first.
The journal covers one current source file up to 250,000 characters per project;
larger files rely on normal browser saves and checkpoints. Browser/site data
removal also removes browser history; it is not cloud backup.

Link a folder using the browser's File System Access picker. Review the save
plan before writing. Existing unknown differences and external edits are
conflicts; the tool refuses them. Save checks again before each file and never
deletes absent files. Folder handles are retained when supported, and permission
may be requested again after reopening. Download backup is available when the
picker is unsupported. File saves are atomic per file, not across an entire
project; a filesystem failure may leave some reviewed files saved.

## 5. Test explorer

Tests discovers project files ending in `.tests.json`. Run one case or all cases,
stop pending runs, inspect exact expected/actual output and its first difference,
and navigate to a diagnostic or the entry source. Tests compile and execute in
isolated VM workers using the existing sandbox/time limits. They do not execute
arbitrary host commands. A stopped or unavailable run is not marked passed.

**Open example test project** creates a separate workspace containing the seven
existing language examples and their exact-output cases. Your previous project
is preserved. New test case writes a suite for the active entry.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "entry": "main.jimsabz",
  "cases": [
    { "name": "Sum", "inputs": ["7", "5"], "expectedOutput": "A: B: 12\n" }
  ]
}
```

Entry paths are workspace-relative. Each suite allows 1–20 cases. Prompts and
final newlines count as output. Error cases may specify `expectedError` instead.
The explorer executes Jimsabz project tests; the source package's Node/C++
regression suites continue to run from the development terminal.

## 6. Local Git integration

Install Git and Node 20+, then start from the Studio package:

```powershell
node api/server.mjs --workspace "C:\path\to\your-project"
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:45426` and choose Source control. Supported operations are
repository initialization, status, working/staged diffs, selected-file staging
and unstaging, local commit history, branch listing, branch creation and switching.
Review the staged diff, enter your author name/email and write a message before
creating a local commit. Identity overrides apply to that commit only; repository
and global Git configuration stay unchanged.
A stale staged revision is refused. Branch changes require a clean working tree.
No push, reset, clean, remote operation or branch deletion endpoint is provided.

The folder must be the repository root. Import disk project creates a new browser
workspace; the prior workspace is retained. Review save to disk uses imported
file hashes and refuses external differences. Missing browser files are retained
on disk. After switching branches, import the disk project to refresh the editor.
Text/asset import is bounded to 256 files / 12 MiB; a single file is limited to

4 MiB. Saves are bounded to 8 MiB total and checked before each write.

Local endpoints enforce loopback, same-origin checks and a per-server session
token. Source paths are restricted to the selected root; linked directories,
private dot paths and executables are refused. Git uses argument arrays with no
shell, bounded output/timeouts and disabled repository hooks/clean/smudge/process
filters. Commit signing is left to a separate normal Git workflow. The agent has
no autonomous Git or shell tool. The hosted preview cannot access local repositories.

## 7. Scene and asset editor

Open a game source and choose Scene & assets. Add a primitive object, select it,
edit literal position/scale/dimensions/color/shape, or drag it on the placement
canvas. A 3D scene uses top-down X/Z placement and a Y property field. Arrow keys
move the selected object; Shift increases the step. Bounding-box overlays help
with placement. The preview initializes the actual compiled scene in an isolated
VM and draws its snapshot with the existing renderer.

Edits stay in a draft. Compile & apply checks the draft against the project and
refuses stale source. A recovery checkpoint precedes application. Existing game
events and non-edited source are preserved. Expression-based properties require
source editing. This first editor does not provide animation/tilemap painting,
mesh modeling, a physics simulation editor or a replacement for the Run window.
Preview does not measure frame rate, audio or interactive gameplay.

The asset inventory previews images/audio and shows model source, references,
missing resources and unreferenced candidates. Static analysis cannot prove that
an asset is unused when paths are generated dynamically; candidates are not
deleted. Parse failures mark the scan incomplete.

## 8. Usability and accessibility

Project, agent and compiler dividers support pointer dragging and keyboard
arrows, with sizes saved in this browser. Develop > Workspace resets panel sizes.
Display & keyboard settings provides larger editor text, higher contrast and
reduced interface motion. Existing dark/light themes are retained. Dialogs use
native focus containment, named controls, keyboard tab navigation and status
messages. A skip link focuses the main workspace. Responsive styles adapt the
tools to narrower displays; mobile execution remains separately unverified.

## Development checks

```text
npm run test:professional
node --test --test-concurrency=2 tests/*.test.mjs
npm run test:release
```

The existing native/compiler/VM tests remain authoritative for language behavior.
Release-specific results are recorded under `docs/validation/` and in
`MADADGAR-RELEASE.json`. Statuses describe executed checks only.

# Local Code Madadgar implementation profile — Studio 0.19.0

This profile describes the actual local agent and takes priority over generic
capability claims in the creator brief. The brief targets v2.5; the package
retains the native C++ compiler/runtime 0.8.0, stack VM, browser compiler/VM,
JBC2/JBC3 metadata and implemented v3 preview. V3-LANGUAGE.md describes the
preview, and LANGUAGE.md describes the retained v2.6 baseline. Existing programs
are not silently downgraded.

## Language facts

- `.jimsabz` is source; `.jbc` is compiler bytecode.
- `adad` is a checked signed 64-bit integer; `dec` is a finite decimal value;
  `lafz` is text; `isharo` is Boolean (`ha` / `na`). `isharo` is not a character
  type in this implementation.
- Input is `budh("Prompt: ")`; output is `budhai expression`, `budhai(expression)`
  or `budhai = expression`. `budha` remains a compatibility output alias.
- Functions use `kam name(adad value) -> adad { wapas value }`.
- Dynamic arrays use `qatar adad values = []`, `values.joryo(value)`,
  `values.lambai`, indexing and `gin value andar values { ... }`.
- The actual seven phases are lexical analysis, syntax analysis, AST,
  semantic analysis, code generation, assets and runtime. Compilation alone
  leaves runtime Ready/Not Run.
- The v3 guide documents inheritance, interfaces, generics, closures, named and
  variadic arguments, collections and cooperative tasks. These are preview
  contracts, not a claim about an older v2.5 specification.

## Built-in local agent

Code Madadgar is ready when Studio opens. Its local trained intent classifier,
parameterized code generators, language question/answer data, versioned lexical
retrieval and compiler-driven actions do not require an external inference
service, account, API key or model installation. The native launcher has no

model-server proxy. Provider selection and connection settings have been removed.

The bundled classifier is trained on 380 requests with 117 held-out requests
from the included 497-target curriculum. It supports 15 generator intents:
marks, percentage, local login, output, input, sum, conditions, loops, functions,
arrays, a 2D player, a 3D scene, 2D racing, numeric statistics and classes/objects.
Raw classifier accuracy on this expanded curated evaluation is 100/117 (85.5%).
The compiler-checked request planner, spelling normalization and explicit
requirements routing are separate from that raw classifier score. The training run was performed for Studio 0.14.0 and the classifier is reused
unchanged in 0.18.0; chats and attachments do not automatically train it.

Simple percentages honor the requested count, including “two inputs of marks”.
Two subject marks default to 100 each; obtained/total wording selects a ratio
calculator instead. Assumptions are stated. Explicit arrays, functions, average,
maxima and runtime counts are preserved. Common typos and “could you please”
wrappers are normalized without changing quoted strings or fenced source.

Login requests generate a working, temporary local account flow with bounded
attempts. Gaming-hub requests add native 3D Home/Arena/Library/Profile gallery
views, guarded navigation and sign out. The compiler/runtime has console input,
keyboard events and HUD text; it has no masked-password or editable GUI form API.
The demo uses visible console passphrases and memory-only accounts. It is not
production authentication: password hashing, a persistent account service,
server-side sessions and complete playable hub games are not implemented.

Responses display complete generated source in expandable Copy code cards.
Selected new builders include exact-output example fixtures run in the real VM;

a failing example disables Apply. Otherwise runtime and tests remain Not Run.
Architecture questions produce an explanation without staging source.

Subject/input counts are parsed from requests or read at runtime. Arrays,
loops and functions support 7, 12, 1000 or runtime-selected counts; the language
is not restricted to three inputs. It is still a constrained local agent, not
an unrestricted generative language model. Unsupported code synthesis is
explained. Supplied Jimsabz source can use all supported compiler features.

Twenty-six local backend interfaces provide file reads/search, staged text edits,
rename/import rewrites, Trash, entry selection, project analysis, documentation
and example retrieval, plans/notes, compilation, bytecode inspection, run inputs
and expected-output tests. No external model selects or executes tools. The local
coordinator performs supported actions in sequence. Shell, Git, web research,
remote providers and arbitrary OS filesystem agent access are unavailable.

## Verification and repair

The local compiler and VM produce actual diagnostics, output and test results.
Automatic repair handles missing required imports, unmatched closing blocks
using lexer tokens, and the old input spelling. A candidate must compile in
the complete project snapshot before Apply is enabled. Unknown repairs are
explained; successful behavior or execution is never fabricated.

A draft cannot overwrite a changed live source snapshot. Review precedes Apply;
Undo preserves later unrelated project notes and refuses later source edits.
Private paths are excluded, and potential credentials are filtered from stored
conversation text and rejected in notes/drafts. This pattern-based filter is not
an exhaustive secret detector. Source paths remain relative to the workspace.

Execution uses isolated workers with an 8-second timeout plus VM limits.
There are at most 1,000 files / 32 MB of snapshot data, 2,000 supplied inputs,
60,000 output characters, 120 headless ticks and 20 expected-output/error cases
per test call. Runtime writes are discarded; networking is disabled. These
limits are not OS CPU/memory quotas. Native C++ execution, Windows behavior,
rendering, audio and frame rate require separate checks. The creator brief's
60 FPS, 300 entities, 500 particles, <64 MB and <50 ms remain targets until measured.

Knowledge references retain their source, version and exact source lines.
Retrieval uses BM25 plus deterministic token-hash vectors, not learned semantic
embeddings. Attached reports remain unverified requirements data. Existing PDF,
DOCX and speech adapters are retained; optional browser speech may use network.


## Studio 0.18 professional tools

PROFESSIONAL-0.18.0.md describes the current editor, recovery, test explorer,
local Git API, scene editor, release scripts and accessibility features.
A compositional numeric planner adds min/max, median, heapsort and search in
reusable multi-file projects, with compiler/VM sample verification. A calculator
builder checks arithmetic and zero division. These supplement the existing 15
classifier intents and do not constitute unrestricted model-based generation.
Git is available through explicit IDE controls on the configured local server;
the agent still has no shell or Git tool. The native compiler and Run window
implementation are retained. Windows execution and publisher signing remain
Not Run in this Linux development session.


## Compiler Factory (Studio 0.19.0)

Run Code opens the integrated Compiler Factory in the existing separate Run window. The real compiler produces six phase states and actual artifacts; the existing VM waits for the journey handoff or Run now. See COMPILER-FACTORY-0.19.0.md for controls, exact tree semantics, evidence limits and verification. The compiler grammar, analyzer and VM implementation are unchanged.

# Jimsabz language v3.0 preview — Studio 0.10.0

This release extends the existing C++ compiler and stack VM. It retains .jimsabz source, newline-separated statements, curly braces, budh input, budhai output, Roman Sindhi/Unicode aliases, game constructs and the native 2D/3D runtime. New attributes use explicit contextual labels; no unreviewed Sindhi translations have been invented.

## What is implemented

| Capability | Syntax and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Inheritance | `qism Child : Base, Named` — one class base, multiple interfaces; base fields precede derived fields |
| Interfaces | `@interface qism Named { kam name() -> lafz }`; concrete classes must implement required methods |
| Polymorphism | `@virtual`, `@override`, `@abstract`, `@final`; runtime dispatch preserves actual object type through a base/interface reference |
| Encapsulation | `@public` (default), `@private`, `@protected` on fields/methods; checked access follows declaring class |
| Constructors | `kam naon(adad value = 0) { ... }`; synchronous, khali-returning, positional fixed parameters; field defaults run in declaration/global scope before the body |
| Base construction | If a base has a custom constructor, each derived constructor must start with `paan[Base].naon(...)`; missing initialization is SEM-143 |
| Function parameters | Defaults, named arguments, final variadic parameter `adad ...values`, array spread `...values`; positional arguments precede named arguments |
| Overloading | Signature selection prefers exact parameter types over widening; ambiguity and duplicate signatures are errors |
| Function values | `kam(adad)->adad f = ...`; typed function references and bound methods |
| Closures | Local kam declarations and `kam(adad x)->adad => x*2`; lexical variables captured by shared cell, including mutation after the outer call returns |

| Generics | `kam identity<T>(T value) -> T`, `qism Box<T>`; inferred function arguments or explicit `identity::<adad>(7)` |
| Constraints | `T: Numeric`, `Comparable`, `Hashable`, or nominal class/interface constraint; bounded compile-time specialization |
| Dictionaries | `Map<lafz,adad> m = naon Map<lafz,adad>()`, after `kharna Collections` |
| Sets | `Set<lafz> s = naon Set<lafz>()`; duplicate add returns na; insertion order retained |
| Nullable values | `adad? value`, `khali`, `??` fallback, checked `Core.unwrap(value)`; no flow narrowing or optional chaining |
| Collections | Map set/get/tryGet/has/remove/keys/values/clear; Set add/contains/remove/values/keys/clear; primitive keys; 0-based arrays with map/filter/reduce/insert/reverse/contains |
| Iteration | `gin key andar dictionary` iterates keys; set iterates values; arrays iterate elements. Structural changes during iteration/callbacks raise a catchable fault. Keys/values snapshots can be iterated independently. |
| Async | `@async kam`, `Task<T>`, `@await`, non-blocking `Async.sleep(seconds)`, `Async.run(task)` console boundary, cancel/isDone |
| Debugger | IDE Debug button; pause at entry, breakpoints, step into/over/out, call stack, selected-frame variables, source navigation; native JSON pause events |

Existing typed arrays and record construction remain supported. A class without a custom constructor still accepts fields in declaration order, omitting trailing defaults.

## Important rules

Explicit call arguments evaluate left to right, then omitted defaults evaluate in parameter order, once per call. Earlier parameter values are available in later defaults. A required parameter cannot follow a default; only the final parameter can be variadic. Named/spread calls through a plain function type do not retain declaration metadata. Generic functions specialize from exact inferred types; explicit types can request permitted numeric widening. Generic methods/local generic declarations, variance, partial specialization and first-class generic function values are not implemented.

Closures retain references to lexical bindings. Separate outer calls create independent captured bindings. Native C++ shared ownership is supplemented by iterative tracing of VM roots to break unreachable cycles; collection does not move objects or run user finalizers. Embedders retaining a Value outside VM state must pin it in VM.hostRoots. No user-level destructor/RAII syntax or hard real-time GC guarantee is provided.

The async scheduler resumes task frames cooperatively on one VM thread, with a 10,000-instruction quantum and an overall instruction budget. Game clocks drive timers while games run. Await suspends a task; Async.run is rejected on an active game loop. Native async file operations use bounded host workers and copy only path/text into them. Cancellation stops further task execution and raises RUN-TASK-CANCEL when observed. A file write already started may finish after cancellation. Task cancellation does not roll back external work. Console programs must explicitly wait for tasks they need; exiting a program does not wait forever on unobserved tasks. Thread creation, mutexes, channels, parallel language execution, async networking and structured task groups remain future work.

Map/Set keys are adad, dec, lafz or isharo. A missing Map.get throws; Map.tryGet returns T?. Mapping iteration follows insertion order, not sorted order. Bounds, key, arity, mutation and immutable-alias failures are checked. Containers are bounded to one million entries. Array length and collection size are read-only. Array map/filter/reduce callbacks are synchronous, statically typed functions. Replacing a dictionary value does not invalidate its key iterator; adding/removing keys does.

## Standard library contracts

Import each namespace with `kharna Namespace`. Existing gui/gui3d/audio/hisab/waqt/shabak imports remain available. The following table is the actual implemented API, not a future wish list. Types are checked at compile time; runtime I/O and invalid operations raise faults handled by azmai/pakar.

| Module | Functions and return types | Error/implementation notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Core | typeName(value): lafz; text(value): lafz; unwrap(T?): T | unwrap(khali) fails; introspection does not introduce unchecked Any variables |
| Math | sqrt/sin/cos/abs(dec): dec; min/max/pow(dec,dec): dec; clamp(dec,dec,dec): dec; floor/round(dec): adad | Integer widening allowed; non-finite results, overflow, invalid clamp bounds fail. Rounding halves away from zero. |

| + - | left |
| * / % | left |
| unary + - ! naheen @await, prefix ++ -- | right |
| calls, member/index, postfix ++ -- | left |

## Compiler, AST and bytecode

The lexer recognizes @, ?, ??, =>, :: and .... Parser nodes retain defaults, generic parameters, constraints, bases, attributes and type arguments. The semantic elaborator specializes generic classes, flattens inherited fields/methods, checks contracts and resolves stable method slots. Semantic analysis adds lexical callable symbols, overload binding, generic function instantiation, nominal conversions and Task/nullable checks. New nodes are lambda, await, spread and baseview; local functions retain lexical environments. Code generation emits callable captures, indirect calls, labeled calls and suspension points. The runtime retains suspended task stack/environment/PC/traps and typed defaults.

JBC3 preserves existing opcodes 0..29 and adds CLOSURE=30, INVOKE=31, CALL_NAMED=32, AWAIT=33. CLOSURE uses mode 0 for global, 1 for lexical, 2 for bound method; its text identifies a function/method slot. INVOKE takes the callable below N arguments; CALL_NAMED names the function. Call labels are U+001F-separated strings (empty positional label; `*` spread). AWAIT consumes a Task and eventually pushes its result. Function records add flags (variadic=1, async=2), signature and parameter-default instruction vectors. Class records add abstract/interface flags and transitive parent names. Header is JIMJBC3 followed by newline, payload byte length and CRC32. The standalone JIMEXE2 trailer can wrap JBC3. Programs requiring no new metadata/opcodes remain JBC2. New readers accept both; old readers reject JBC3. A control-flow verifier checks reachable operand stack heights, jumps, opcode/metadata bounds and await placement; runtime conversions and checks remain necessary. This is not a proof of full type-safety of arbitrary hostile bytecode.

## Debugging

In Studio click **Debug**. The run window pauses before execution. Continue (F5), Step over (F10), Step into (F11), Step out and Show source operate on the live VM. Select a call-stack frame to inspect its visible variables. Enter `main.jimsabz:8, modules/math.jimsabz:12` to set breakpoints, then Continue. Line stepping pauses on source-line/frame changes; a one-line loop has coarse stepping. Local variables do not appear until their declarations execute. Stop terminates the worker. Changing source requires restarting the debug session.

Native CLI: `build/jimsabz debug examples/v3/escaping-mutable-closure.jimsabz`. Pause events are JSON lines on stderr; ordinary program output stays on stdout. Send `step`, `next`, `out`, `continue`, `break file.jimsabz:line`, `clear file.jimsabz:line` or `quit` on stdin. Program input uses the same stream once resumed. This is an embeddable CLI protocol, not a DAP server. Native runtime faults include function call sites. There is no full VS Code LSP/DAP extension, expression watch evaluator, symbol refactoring, reverse debugging or native multithread debugger yet.

## Compatibility and tests

The release preserves existing program and game tests. Correct named argument binding replaces the old behavior that discarded labels; callers that relied on ignored/misspelled labels must fix them. Existing qism field constructors and defaults remain. Array iteration now detects structural mutation; iterate a snapshot or change elements without changing size/order. v3 defaults/closures/async programs use JBC3 and need runtime 0.8.0. No automatic project conversion is required. Legacy mahfooz snapshots do not serialize function values, tasks or Map/Set containers; save their plain data explicitly.

`tests/v3-cases.json` is the shared source/expected-output/negative fixture catalog. `python tests/v3_features.py` executes native source and native-compiled bytecode; `node tests/v3-browser.test.mjs` executes browser source and browser-produced bytecode in the native VM. `tests/debugger.test.mjs` drives the real VM/controller, and `tests/v3_runtime.cpp` exercises escaping closures, cyclic data and non-blocking game ticks under sanitizers. Original regression/runtime/UI suites remain required. Windows binaries are cross-compiled here; interactive execution on Windows must be checked on Windows.

## Working examples

Use the **v3 examples** button to open an independent file without overwriting existing work. Portable sources are included under examples/v3. The examples cover each implemented feature and import the actual libraries they use. They are console language demonstrations; game projects still begin from blank 2D/3D templates.

# Jimsabz language v2.6 — Studio 0.9.0

Files are UTF-8 and use `.jimsabz`. Identifiers are case-sensitive. A newline ends a statement; only `gin` loop headers use semicolons. Blocks use `{ ... }`. Comments use `//` or `/* ... */`.

## Types and expressions

```jimsabz
adad count = 7
dec speed = 3.5
lafz name = "Farhan"
isharo alive = ha
pakko adad LIMIT = 100
qatar adad values = [10, 20, 30]
qatar qatar adad grid = [[1, 2], [3, 4]]
```

Uninitialized primitive variables receive zero, false, or an empty string. Arrays are dynamic. `values.lambai`, `values.joryo(40)` and `values.kadh(0)` get length, append, and remove/return an element. Out-of-range indices raise a runtime fault. A `pakko` container and its shared contents are immutable.

`adad` uses checked signed 64-bit arithmetic. Integer division truncates toward zero. `dec` uses finite double-precision values. Integers widen to decimals; decimals require `badal(value, adad)` to narrow. String concatenation formats a primitive value when the left operand is `lafz`.

Precedence, highest first: member/index/call/grouping/postfix increment; prefix increment/sign/negation; `* / %`; `+ -`; ordering; equality; AND; OR; assignment. Assignment is right-associative. AND/OR short-circuit. Other operands and arguments evaluate left to right.

| Symbol | Sindhi-inspired alias |
| --- | --- |
| `==` | `barabar` |
| `!=` | `na_barabar` |
| `>` | `wado` |
| `<` | `nandho` |
| `>=` | `wado_barabar` |
| `<=` | `nandho_barabar` |
| `&&` | `ain` |
| `\|\|` | `ya` |
| `!` | `naheen` |

## Input and output

```jimsabz
lafz name = budh("Name: ")
adad age = budh("Age: ")
budhai name + " is " + age
```

Input converts to the target primitive type at assignment. Boolean input accepts `ha`/`na`, `true`/`false`, or `1`/`0`. Invalid numbers and a closed input stream raise catchable runtime faults.

# Code Madadgar — the built-in local Jimsabz agent

## Start

1. Extract the complete ZIP.
2. Run `Start-Studio.cmd` on Windows 11.
3. Open **Code Madadgar** and type a request. The agent is ready immediately.

The included classifier, generators, documentation and compiler/VM perform the
agent work locally. There is no model-server setup, provider selection, external
AI API, account, API key or downloaded language model. Once the ZIP is on your
computer, the agent does not need internet. Optional browser speech recognition
may use the browser's speech service; typing always remains available.

## Requests to try

| Request | Local behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Write a simple program that takes two inputs of marks and their precentage` | Exactly two subject inputs; percentage out of 200, with a stated assumption |
| `Read obtained marks and total marks and calculate percentage` | Two-value ratio calculator with validation |
| `Build a gaming hub with local login and 3D UI architecture` | Complete local demo project, native 3D gallery navigation and explicit production gaps |
| `Explain the gaming hub architecture` | Architecture answer without modifying project files |
| `Write a program that prints "Farhan"` | Generate checked Jimsabz source as a new draft |
| `Write a marksheet for 7 subjects with average` | Functions, arrays, marks, percentage, average and grade |
| `Change to 12 subjects with average` | Adapt the previous generator request and preserve old source |
| `Write a marksheet that asks how many subjects at runtime` | Let the program's user choose its input count |
| `Sum 1000 numbers and calculate their average using an array` | Reusable array/function/loop code with the requested count |
| `Create a class with methods to process many numeric inputs` | Checked class, array and method example |

| `Explain arrays in Jimsabz` | Grounded language help and retrieved sources |
| `Explain this code` | Inspect active source and describe its constructs with compiler evidence |
| `Check my code` | Run lexer, parser, AST, semantics, bytecode and asset checks |
| `Fix my code` | Attempt one supported, compiler-verified repair in a draft |
| `Analyze my project` | Summarize the actual entry, source paths and line counts |
| `Inspect bytecode` | Display actual stack instructions for the active source |
| `Create a controllable 2D player` | Generate the supported player starter |
| `Create a basic 3D scene` | Generate the supported 3D starter |

For interactive input and graphics, use the ordinary **Run code** button. For
an agent-run fixture, provide the inputs explicitly:

```text
Run my code with inputs: ["7", "5"]
```

For a test, state the expected output exactly, including prompts and newlines:

```text
Test my code with inputs: ["7", "5"] expected output: "12\n"
```

The test example expects a program that reads two values without printing prompts.
The agent reports actual output, mismatches and input errors. It never invents
missing input values or marks an unexecuted test as passed.

You can also supply arbitrary supported Jimsabz source, including v3 features:

````text
Use this source as identity.jimsabz:
```jimsabz
kam identity<T>(T value) -> T { wapas value }
budhai identity(42)
```
````

The supplied source is compiled in the complete project snapshot. A compiler
failure leaves a draft with Apply disabled. To explicitly replace the active
source rather than create a new file, begin with `Replace my current program`.

## Review and controls

Generated source is visible directly in the response. Expand a filename and use **Copy code**, or choose **Review changes**. Small programs open automatically.

Generated files and repairs stay in an isolated draft. **Review changes** shows
the exact text changes, entry changes and real verification status. **Apply
changes** checks that the live project still matches the original snapshot.
A stale draft cannot overwrite subsequent source edits. **Reject changes**
preserves the live project. **Undo agent edit** restores the last apply while
its resulting files still match. Deleted draft files go to the existing Trash.

**Knowledge** searches versioned references. **Project notes** and **History**
inspect or clear the current workspace's notes and conversations. **Activity**
shows actual local actions. **Stop** cancels the request and terminates an active
execution worker. **Retry** repeats the last request locally.

Source changes affect the Studio browser working copy. Use Save file or Export
folder for a disk copy. Notes and chat history are browser workspace metadata;
they are not included in a normal source-folder export. Pending in-memory drafts
are lost on tab reload; already-saved source remains intact.

Reports can be attached as PDF, DOCX or text. Supported requirements generate a
reviewed project subfolder; the included PROJECT-PLAN.md identifies remaining work.
A generated starter is not a claim that every report requirement is implemented.

## Automatic repair scope

The local repair rules handle a compiler-reported missing library import,
unmatched closing blocks detected through lexer tokens, and legacy input
assignments that need `budh(...)`. Each candidate is checked against the real
complete-project compiler. Unsupported diagnostics are explained with their
source file and location; the agent does not invent a repair. Logic changes
need a specific expected behavior and a supported generator or supplied code.

## What was trained

The shipped model is a multinomial Naive Bayes intent classifier with a token
continuation model. Its included corpus has 497 compiler-validated targets:
380 training requests and 117 held-out requests, across 15 supported generator
intents. This release runs new local training. Raw classifier accuracy is
100/117 (85.5%) on the expanded curated set. Requirements routing and spelling
normalization are separate from that score. This does not measure unrestricted
programming skill; no general generative language model was fine-tuned.

English and existing Roman Urdu/Sindhi request routing are included, along with
implemented language help and number vocabulary. The classifier cannot freely
invent an arbitrary application or game from any prose request. Unsupported
requests explain the available alternatives. The Jimsabz compiler itself retains
its existing language features. Source in a jimsabz code block can use those
features even when there is no dedicated natural-language generator.

The trainer, curriculum and evaluation files remain in `training/`. Chat and
attached reports do not silently retrain the model.

## Architecture and limits

`local-agent.mjs` coordinates the local request router, existing trained model,
generators, retrieved references and real tools. `tools.mjs` validates 26 local
backend interfaces; there is no external tool-calling model. `changes.mjs`
implements isolated drafts, path checks, diffs, stale checks and undo.
`execution.mjs` and its worker run the actual Studio compiler and stack VM.
`retrieval.mjs` combines BM25 with deterministic lexical hash vectors; it is not
a learned semantic embedding service. `panel.mjs` provides a single local agent
interface, without a provider/mode selector or model connection settings.

Execution workers have an 8-second outer timeout plus existing VM instruction

and call-depth limits. A snapshot accepts up to 1,000 files and 32 MB of data.
A run accepts up to 2,000 inputs, 60,000 output characters and 120 headless game
ticks. A test call accepts 1–20 explicit expected-output/error cases. Runtime
file writes remain in the isolated snapshot and are discarded. Agent runs have
no LAN access. Headless game checks do not measure graphics, sound, controls,
FPS or Windows behavior. These are application limits, not OS resource quotas.

The native C++ launcher serves local static files and startup/heartbeat routes.
It has no external inference proxy or model-server connection endpoint.
The agent executes the Studio browser compiler/VM; native compiler/VM execution
and bytecode interoperability are checked separately by repository tests.

## Developer checks

```text
node scripts/build-madadgar-knowledge.mjs
node tests/madadgar.test.mjs
node tests/madadgar-worker.test.mjs
```

The agent suite uses the actual bundled classifier and actual compiler/VM. Its
local-generation network test rejects all fetch calls while generation runs.
There are no scripted external model replies in the local agent suite.
See MADADGAR-VALIDATION.md for executed results and platform limits.

## Local login boundary

Create a temporary user and invented passphrase in the separate Run console,
then sign in with those values. Passphrases are visible. Accounts are not saved
to disk. A failed login never initializes the 3D hub. A successful login opens
Home; click Game and use 1 / 2 / 3 to select sections, H for Home and L to sign
out. Signed-out sessions cannot navigate back in; Run again resets the demo.
The sections are 3D gallery previews, not complete games. A real account service,
password hashing, protected server sessions and graphical password fields remain
separate implementation work.
